$comment: CANONICAL source policy (requirements §6). Single source of truth. Consumed deterministically by scripts/source-check.sh (via the `signals` arrays) and read as guidance by skills/step-2-research and agents/adversarial-reviewer (via `categories`). Edit HERE only — do not re-hardcode these lists anywhere else. Per-run overrides still come from controls.source_policy / source_quality_threshold.

blacklist.description: Never rely on these, and never cite them as a load-bearing source.
categories: personal or company blogs and opinion posts
content farms, SEO filler, and undated aggregators
circular sources (many outlets all quoting one unverified origin)
forums and social posts as evidence (usable only as leads to trace to a primary source)
blacklist.$comment: TYPE/TIER descriptors only — matched as substrings against a source's tier+citation string. Platform NAMES (reddit, quora, twitter, …) belong in blocked_domains, NOT here, to avoid substring false positives (e.g. 'social' matching 'social science', 'reddit' matching 'notreddit.com').

whitelist.description: Actively seek and prefer these; a load-bearing claim must rest on one.
categories: primary data and official statistical / records sources (read critically, never as propaganda)
the primary document behind a claim (the actual study / dataset / filing)

tiering.rule: Every source carries a quality tier. A LOAD-BEARING claim must rest on a whitelisted, sufficiently-high tier meeting the run's source_quality_threshold. If only a blacklisted or low/unknown-tier source exists for a load-bearing claim, that claim is treated as UNSUPPORTED — independently re-sourced or cut (routes per §5.2).

blocked_domains.description: HARD block by domain. A source on any of these domains (or a subdomain of one) is rejected outright — for ANY claim, load-bearing or not, regardless of tier. These may still be used privately as a lead to trace to a primary source, but must NEVER be cited as the source. Matching is host-suffix based: 'reddit.com' also blocks 'www.reddit.com' and 'old.reddit.com'; 'wikipedia.org' blocks 'en.wikipedia.org' etc.

blocked_url_patterns.description: HARD block by substring/pattern matched anywhere in a source's URL or citation string. Use for path-based or non-domain blocks (e.g. '/blog/', 'sponsored'). Case-insensitive substring match. Empty by default.

preferred_domains.description: Domains to actively PREFER when choosing among candidate sources (guidance for the research and review agents; not hard-enforced by source-check.sh). Suffix-based like blocked_domains; '.gov' / '.edu' match any government / educational host.
